backstory:
Calla Vond keeps a gunsmith's bench under the sign of the golden key, and every barrel she rifles is stamped twice: once with her maker's mark, once with the seal of the Guild of Abadar that takes its tithe of her every sale. She is a fine shot, but she will tell you the craft is in the boring of the bore, not the pulling of the trigger.

She came up the way most Sojorian tradesfolk do, apprenticed young and bound to her master's debts before she was tall enough to see over his lathe. The Bank advanced the price of her tools against ten years of her wages; the Guild found her a stall once the loan was clear. Her people, three generations of Vonds, have all banked with Abadar and prayed to him in the same breath, for in Sojoria the church and the counting-house keep the same hours.

She trusts a signed contract over a sworn oath and a balanced ledger over a friend, and she thinks the hundred-year war with Feyador a great waste of good powder. Still, war sells guns, and Abadar teaches that profit honestly got is its own kind of grace.

Personality: shrewd, precise, dryly funny.
Mannerisms: walks a coin across her knuckles while she thinks.
Appearance: powder-burned cuffs and a jeweler's loupe always pushed up on her brow.
Flaws: cannot resist a sure profit, even one that looks a little dishonest.
